overall_summary: The sample size of 10 videos is too small to establish definitive long-term viral patterns, though a slight positive lean is observed in content balancing self-respect with digital boundary milestones like deleting chats or blocking numbers.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on concrete digital actions like chat deletion and self-respect (e.g., AfaLxMy6FMY) garnered the highest views in the dataset (33 views).
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate tangible smartphone habits and personal boundaries into the narrative arc.

weak_patterns.evidence: Openings like 'रात के दो बजे' (G0gKV1p3ZHc) or tea-related metaphors (uIbMpCjVutQ) resulted in lower initial traction (5-12 views).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid abstract time-of-night clichés; ground the beginning in a specific, physical action or device notification.

next_video.concept: Removing someone from a favorite contact widget on the phone home screen.
next_video.opening_direction: Widgets pe unka photo hatane ki koshish...
next_video.twist_direction: Realizing that removing the shortcut finally freed up space on the home screen for yourself.
next_video.reason: Previous relative peak performance (AfaLxMy6FMY) occurred around the early afternoon publishing slot, focusing on self-respect themes.

experiment: Testing if shifting the focus from passive late-night longing to active home-screen digital decluttering improves early viewer retention and view velocity.
